SMTO-SKL-0101 — That Microsoft 365 change clashes with something already there

GUID: 706a2f71-fa5d-5617-b322-320603d04a95
Slug: microsoft365-resource-conflict
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • Microsoft turned the change down because it clashes with what's already there, most often a file or folder with the same name in the same place.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to list what's in the destination folder, or open it in OneDrive or Outlook. You'll see the existing item that the change clashes with.
  2. Ask the Agent to use a different name or location for your item. A unique name avoids the clash without touching the existing item.
  3. If you really mean to overwrite the existing file, ask the Agent to look it up first and then replace it. Replacing needs the current version so nothing is overwritten by accident.

What success looks like

  • The Agent reports the change as done and you can see it in OneDrive or Outlook.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with the name and place you were using.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft Graph rejected the request with HTTP 409 or ErrorIrresolvableConflict (for example an existing item with the same name under conflictBehavior=fail).

What this means

  • Graph returns HTTP 409 or ErrorIrresolvableConflict. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Graph returns HTTP 409 or ErrorIrresolvableConflict.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact destination and existing item before choosing replacement or a new name.

How to fix it

  • Read the current state of the target (list the parent folder or read the item) and choose a non-conflicting name or destination, or deliberately replace the existing item (file_upload with conflict=replace and its observed etag). The 409 was a definite rejection, so confirm the target state rather than replaying the same request.
  • Read current provider state and choose a nonconflicting destination or review the existing item before replacing it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate operation resolves the actual conflict without duplicating work.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
